title: Unification & Adaptation Blueprint: Transitioning legacy protocols to the Unified Inference API
creator: Anika Rao
description: High-level blueprint for converging legacy streaming and tokenized model endpoints onto the Unified Inference API while minimizing client disruption. This document defines requirements, acceptable adaptation approaches (client SDK shim vs. server-side compatibility), rollout stages, acceptance criteria, and monitoring for a safe, measurable transition.
background: We currently operate multiple legacy protocols (SSE streaming endpoints, long-poll fallbacks, and 'tokenized' model aliases mapping to older runtime variants). These cause operational overhead, split telemetry, and make feature rollouts harder. Rather than an immediate shutdown, the preferred approach is to provide a short-term compatibility bridge and clear client adaptation path to the Unified Inference API so customers and SDKs can migrate predictably.
scope: In-scope: SSE streaming endpoints (stream.v1), long-poll endpoints used by older clients, model aliasing that maps to deprecated runtime variants, and associated docs/SDKs.
Out-of-scope: Hosted-only internal admin endpoints and third-party partner integrations under bespoke contracts (handled by account teams).
Deliverables: compatibility bridge (server-side), SDK shim releases (JS/Python), migration docs, telemetry dashboards, fallback policies, and deprecation messaging cadence.
non_goals: Rewrite the Unified Inference API during this effort; the API contract remains stable.
Forcing immediate client changes — aim is to provide adaptation and observability rather than breaking changes without notice.
requirements: R1: Provide a server-side compatibility bridge that accepts legacy SSE and long-poll requests and translates them to the Unified Inference request model with <2ms median translation latency.
R2: Publish JS and Python SDK shims that map legacy streaming patterns to Unified API streaming or chunked responses with clear config flags and opt-in telemetry.
R3: Distinguish enterprise vs self-serve clients: enterprise customers may request extended compatibility windows via runbooks; self-serve gets the standard timeline.
R4: Instrument migration telemetry: per-client API usage, shim adoption rate, error rate delta, and median end-to-end latency pre/post translation.
R5: Exhaustive acceptance criteria (see acceptance_criteria) must be met before changing default routing to decommission legacy endpoints.
R6: Deprecation messaging: 120/60/30/14/7 day cadence starting when default routing change is announced to clients and on the dashboard.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Compatibility bridge successfully handles 99.5% of incoming legacy requests without behavioral regressions compared to baseline (tokenization, stop sequences, tool-calling semantics).
AC2: SDK shim adoption: >= 50% of legacy-client traffic is routed through official SDK shims within 12 weeks of SDK release; >= 80% within 20 weeks for self-serve tenants.
AC3: No more than 1% increase in 95th-percentile client-observed latency across rolling 72-hour windows after translation is enabled for a given region.
AC4: Error spike threshold: any delta >3x baseline error rate triggers automatic rollback of routing changes for affected shard/region and a P1 incident review within 2 hours.
AC5: Documentation and migration guides are published, reviewed by Developer Experience and Legal, and linked from Console before routing default flips.
AC6: Enterprise customers that opted into extended windows have written runbooks and signed SLAs recorded in customer docs.
migration_guidance: Option A (Recommended): Client update path via official SDK shims. SDKs expose a compatibility flag (e.g., legacyBridge: true) that performs the translation client-side and surfaces matching response shapes. Advantages: lower server complexity, faster client feedback. Trade-off: requires client release coordination.

Option B (Fallback): Server-side compatibility bridge that translates legacy requests to Unified Inference on behalf of clients. Use as default for self-serve migration and for enterprise customers who cannot update immediately. Trade-off: operational complexity and maintenance cost.

Best practices for clients: remove reliance on non-deterministic SSE reconnection behavior (use SDK's resume tokens), migrate stop-sequence handling to explicit structured outputs, and add automated smoke tests comparing legacy vs unified outputs for key prompts.

SDK notes: JS/Python shims must expose diagnostics headers (X-RW-Compat-Mode, X-RW-Shim-Version) and opt-in debug logging. The first SDK release will include a migration helper 'compareLegacy()' to run side-by-side assertions during rollout.
Code sample pointers: provide clear before/after snippets, a short migration checklist with example cURL calls, and a compatibility test harness users can run locally.
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (Prep, 6 weeks): Implement bridge prototype, instrument telemetry pipelines, draft SDK shims, and publish migration docs to staging Confluence. Run internal dogfooding with 3 squads.
Stage 1 (Canary, 2 weeks): Enable bridge for 1% of traffic in a single region. Monitor latency, errors, and functional diffs. Execute rollback playbook if AC3 or AC4 violated.
Stage 2 (Gradual Expansion, 8 weeks): Increase to 10% -> 25% -> 50% across regions with monitoring gates at each step. Announce 120-day deprecation window to clients when 50% achieved.
Stage 3 (SDK push & Client Outreach, 12 weeks): Release stable JS/Python shims, run targeted outreach to largest legacy clients, schedule migration support sessions for enterprise tenants.

Stage 4 (Default routing flip, after acceptance criteria met): Switch default routing to Unified Inference and set compatibility bridge to opt-in via feature flag for remaining clients. Begin final 120->0 day deprecation countdown for bridge removal.
Stage 5 (Deprecation & Cleanup, variable): Remove bridge per customer agreements; close feature flags and decommission legacy endpoints per release schedule.
monitoring_and_kpis: KPI1: Shim adoption rate (percentage of legacy requests using official SDK shims) reported daily.
KPI2: Functional parity metric (percent of translated requests with identical structural outputs) sampled hourly.
KPI3: Client error rate delta and request latency delta (p50/p95/p99) comparing pre-translation baseline.
KPI4: Customer support volume for migration-related tickets and average time-to-resolution.
Dashboards: create 'Legacy->Unified Migration' dashboard in Console with per-tenant drilldowns and a weekly health report emailed to stakeholders.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Translation correctness gaps for niche stop-sequence/tool-calling combinations. Mitigation: build a test corpus from top 200 customers' prompts and run continuous diffing; ship fixes before expanding traffic.
Risk: Increased operational burden and cost from running bridge. Mitigation: implement bridge as lightweight stateless translator with autoscaling limits; cap throughput per tenant during canary.
Risk: SDK adoption is slow for enterprise accounts. Mitigation: dedicate Solutions Engineering to schedule migration workshops and offer extended compatibility windows under written agreements.
Risk: Unexpected security or compliance gaps. Mitigation: mandatory security review (security_review_required=true) and Legal sign-off before default routing flips.
